title: How Off-Plan Real Estate Investing Works: Deposits and Contract Assignment
seoTitle: How Off-Plan Investing Works: Deposits and Assignment
description: How off-plan investors control a $1M unit with a $50K deposit, pay in stages, and assign the contract before completion for a profit.
answer: Developers presell units at low prices to finance construction. You secure a unit with a small first deposit, pay further deposits at construction milestones, and can assign your contract to a new buyer before completion. Your profit is the difference between your price and theirs.
body:
Buying off-plan is one of the biggest opportunities to make money in real estate, and the mechanics are simpler than most people think.

## Why developers presell

A developer needs to sell part of a project before construction to show lenders and investors that the demand is real. To get those first buyers, they offer the best prices the project will ever have. The price is low because the risk is high: nothing has been built yet.

## You secure the unit with a small deposit

You do not pay for the unit up front. At signing you usually pay a small portion of its value. Then the contract sets **milestones**, for example when excavation starts and when the building rises out of the ground, where you add further deposits. Each payment keeps your right to become the owner when the building is complete.

## The contract is a right you can sell

This is the key point. In the presale phase you are not the owner of the property. You own a **right** to buy it at completion, and in most contracts you can transfer that right to someone else. This is called an **assignment**.

## A simple example

- You sign for a unit at **$1,000,000** and pay a first deposit of **$50,000**.
- Twenty months later the building is still under construction, but it is clearly rising.
- Risk has dropped, and similar units now sell for **$1.2 to $1.3 million**.
- You assign your contract to a new buyer at that price. They take over the contract and close the purchase at completion.

You entered when risk was high and the price was low, and you exited when risk was lower and the value was higher. You never owned the property.

## What to check first

Read the assignment clause before you sign. Some developers charge a fee, limit when you can assign, or require their approval. And remember that if the market falls or the project stalls, your deposits are at risk.
takeaways: Developers presell at low prices because early risk is high.
A small first deposit secures the unit; further deposits follow construction milestones.
A presale contract is a right to buy, which you can usually assign to someone else.
Profit comes from the gap between your entry price and the assignment price.
faq: How much deposit do I need to buy off-plan?
It varies by market and developer. A first payment of 5 to 10 percent is common, with further payments tied to construction milestones.
Can I always assign an off-plan contract?
Not always. Check the assignment clause: some developers forbid it, charge a fee, or allow it only after a certain share of units is sold.
What happens if prices fall before completion?
You are still committed to close at your contract price or lose your deposits, which is the main risk of buying off-plan.
